items.name: Growing a Greener Future.Ponce de León Reforestation Project

fields.event-name: Growing a Greener Future.Ponce de León Reforestation Project
fields.event_details:
Our event will be an educational and environmental initiative organised by CEIP Ponce de León, a primary school in Torredonjimeno, Jaén, southern Spain. Its main purpose is to involve children in the restoration of a local green area through tree planting, while raising awareness of climate change, biodiversity and the importance of protecting our natural environment.

The event will bring together pupils and teachers in a meaningful outdoor learning experience, turning environmental awareness into real action. We want our pupils to understand that protecting the planet is not just something we talk about in the classroom, but something we can all contribute to through small, practical actions.

Planned activities and schedule highlights:

1. Welcome and environmental awareness session

The day will begin with a short introduction explaining the importance of forests and green spaces, their role in combating climate change, improving air quality, preventing soil erosion and providing habitats for wildlife. Pupils will learn about the importance of native tree and shrub species and why protecting local biodiversity is essential, particularly in Mediterranean environments such as ours.

2. Getting ready to plant

Teachers will explain the different stages of planting and demonstrate how to prepare the ground, handle young trees and plant them correctly. Pupils will be organised into small groups so that everyone can actively participate. The activity will encourage teamwork, cooperation and responsibility.

3. Hands-on tree planting

This will be the central activity of the event. Working together, pupils and teachers will plant trees and shrubs in the selected area of Torredonjimeno, contributing to the recovery and improvement of a local green space. Each group will take responsibility for planting and identifying its trees, creating a personal connection with the natural environment.

4. Learning through nature

Throughout the activity, pupils will discover the environmental benefits of trees, the importance of native species, the needs of plants and the role that everyone can play in protecting biodiversity. The experience will connect knowledge acquired in the classroom with a real environmental challenge in their own community.

5. A commitment to the future

At the end of the event, pupils will reflect on what they have achieved and make a collective commitment to protecting and caring for the newly planted trees. The school will promote follow-up activities to monitor their growth and encourage long-term environmental responsibility.

Our expected impact:

Beyond the number of trees planted, our greatest goal is to inspire a new generation of environmentally responsible citizens. We want children to feel that they are an active part of the solution to environmental challenges and that their actions can make a difference.

Through this initiative, CEIP Ponce de León aims to strengthen the connection between the school and the local community, contribute to a greener and healthier Torredonjimeno, support biodiversity and promote European values of environmental responsibility and sustainability.

We believe that every tree planted represents a promise for the future, and every child who takes part becomes a seed of positive change.
fields.subscription_instructions: Pupils and teachers of CEIP Ponce de León will take part in the activity. Families and local community members can contact the school for further information.

This event is a replanting day at our two sites in Eberswalde: the Tiny Forest in Rofinpark and the Biodiversity Park in the Technologie- und Gewerbepark Eberswalde. Both sites suffered from the extreme heat and drought of summer 2026 and lost a number of young trees and shrubs. Together with volunteers, we will fill these gaps with saplings grown in our own tree nursery, so that both forests can recover and continue to develop into dense, resilient ecosystems.

Key activities include a short welcome and introduction to the Miyawaki method and the reasons for the losses, a planting demonstration, and the replanting itself in small teams at both sites. We will also water and mulch the new saplings to give them the best possible start.

From 11 to 13 December 2026, volunteers will gather at Finca Mas Mascaró (Corçà, Baix Empordà) to plant 1,000 trees and shrubs in Camp Sech, a syntropic agroforestry system. Syntropic agroforestry is a regenerative model that mimics natural forest succession to rebuild soil, biodiversity and productive landscapes. Professional teams will be present during both days to explain the procedure and support the planting.

The event is promoted by Agro Forestal Mas Mascaró, sponsored by LifeTerra, supported by EU-PFF, and run with Nactiva, Soulfood Forestfarms and AguAbundancia as collaborators and designers of the agroforestry and hidrological systems. This event will turn a weekend in the countryside into a lasting contribution to landscape restoration.

For this second planting event on the Honville project, we welcomed today iSapce EUROPE, an incredibly motivated and cohesive team used to work outside of the realm of Earth's atmosphere. Still, today they engaged themselves to have a tangible action on earth, in the mood of the Belgian countryside to help us plant over 500 trees. Early or punctual, everyone arrived well-prepared, and ready to plant trees, all the way from Luxembourg. While the morning announced a grim day, the sun and blue sky appeared the same time iSpace arrived.

While keeping warm with coffees and snacks, the motivated team of about 40 volunteers started the planting rapidly, efficiently, with a competitive spirit. They had split their team in 5 teams, with the goal to plant the biggest amount of trees, without omitting qualitative work. It was said that the winning team would get a price. SOWoods and I found ourselves with five hyper-motivated teams that started planting like professionals. They almost had them all by lunchtime. They did not waste time at lunch, and before we could even finish eating, they were all back, planting, on the rhythm of house music and immaculate energy. This is probably one of the coolest planting vibe and energy I had the chance to witness. This had a contagious effect on us, making everyone smile and enjoy this beautiful tree planting day!

Before 14h, all the trees were in the ground, and everyone celebrated this great and meaningful accomplishment. I hope to plant trees in these conditions and with such wonderfully motivated teams more often. Thank you iSpace!
